extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing manuscripts to submit to Econometrica (academic economists)
extracted.subtask_description: Official instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting manuscripts, corrections/comments, revisions, and supplemental material to the journal Econometrica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one author must be a member of the Econometric Society to submit a paper. If none of the authors is a member, they must join before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership link provided; submissions from non-members are not allowed unless membership is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous_submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must present original, unpublished work that is not under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A working paper version should be publicly available (personal website or public repository) at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Econometrica accepts only electronic submissions; papers should be submitted in PDF format via the online submission portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickable link provided to start an online submission; recommended (but not required) LaTeX template available from the publisher's support page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission fee applies to all new submissions: US$125 for regular members and US$50 for student members; invited resubmissions require only membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission fee must be paid by credit card at the time of submission; fees are non-refundable, including for papers rejected without review. Individuals in World Bank low-income countries are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will incur a publication fee equal to 50% of the production cost per page, applied to all typeset material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fee is collected after final proofs are approved but before publication and invoiced at prevailing rates. Individuals in World Bank low-income or lower-middle-income countries are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit (main manuscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be limited to 45 pages, including references and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main paper, including any in-paper appendices but excluding the supplemental appendix, must be self-contained. Exceptions to the page limit may be granted only with prior permission from the Editor via email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The font size must be at least 12 points, line spacing at least 1.5, and all margins at least 1.25 inches. These rules apply to the entire manuscript, including references and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended LaTeX template available but not required. Supplemental appendix must follow the same formatting requirements if submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Material should be organized to enhance readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: do not place footnotes and figures at the end of the document; pages should be numbered; title page should include abstract, keywords, and full author affiliations. Abstract must be no more than 150 words; JEL codes are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author order declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Econometrica does not allow the use of \textcircled{r} to indicate a certified random order for authors’ names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are free to specify the methods used to determine author order in a footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental appendix rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include a supplemental appendix with non-essential additional results and robustness analyses that are not critical to the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental appendix should be clearly labeled, should not exceed 25 pages, must follow the same formatting requirements (font size, line spacing, margins) as the main text, and is posted under 'Supplemental Material' and not typeset. The supplemental appendix does not count toward the main paper page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and experimental documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical, experimental, or simulation results require additional supporting documentation per the journal's Replication Policy and Experimental Papers Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation may be submitted with the main paper via the online submission form and does not count toward page limits. Large files should be compressed into a .zip format. If submitting more than two supplemental files, combine them into a single .zip file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and comments: scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal accepts short articles in the form of corrections or comments addressing a paper previously published in the relevant journal; corrections and comments differ in scope and ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correction is a very short article identifying an error or flaw significant enough to merit formal documentation, primarily to restore factual accuracy. A comment is more substantial and may identify shortcomings that undermine validity or provide substantial generalization or improvement while directly building on the published paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and comments: authorship and contact with original authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a correction or comment requires contacting at least one of the original authors unless an original author is part of the submitting team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original authors do not respond within two months, this should be noted in the submission and the correspondence with original authors should be included. The original authors may be invited to reply to any accepted correction or comment. Titles should follow the prescribed format: 'Correction to ‘‘[original paper title]’’' or 'Comment on ‘‘[original paper title]’’'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: An offer to revise a paper is typically valid for 12 months from the decision date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted at the discretion of the handling Co-Editor but must be requested within that 12-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter only if it contains information relevant to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant information includes: details of related work submitted elsewhere; explanation if the submission relates to a previously rejected Econometrica paper and why it is sufficiently different to warrant independent review; any request for exemption from the journal’s Editorial Procedures and Policies must be stated explicitly at the time of initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to editorial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a paper indicates that the authors agree to abide by the journal’s Editorial Procedures and Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information for the Editorial Office is provided for questions.
